original.title: Giant Bug of the Ocean: Sea Scorpions — How Deep Do You Hide? 🦂
original.banner: Giant sea scorpion: where do you hide?
original.hook_vo: A sea scorpion nearly two metres long. Pick a depth.
original.art_direction: Olive-green and bronze estuary palette, murky backlight, low-angle 35mm lens, one warm brass-coloured glow per frame.

options.label: Muddy shoreline shallows
options.vo: One: ankle-deep on a muddy shore.
options.image_prompt: ankle-deep muddy shoreline of a Silurian sea, low mossy green mats on bare rock, olive water, one warm brass-coloured sunset glow on the ripples, photoreal painterly, vertical composition

options.label: Knee-deep in the shallows
options.image_prompt: Three small living Eurypterus swim just above a pale mud bed in shallow olive Silurian water. Use the supplied fossil as the body-plan guide: one broad low head shield with paired crescent eyes, an elongated flattened segmented abdomen tapering into one straight pointed terminal spine, small jointed walking legs tucked close beneath the front body and one conspicuous pair of broad flat rear swimming appendages. One complete animal is clearly visible in elevated side view at the lower left, with two much smaller separate animals in the midground. All three remain horizontal and fully submerged. Matte brown natural exoskeleton, fine suspended silt, a restrained warm amber sun glow on the near muddy floor. Only living animals, sediment and water replace the fossil slab.
options.art_direction: Elevated underwater view of three small flat brown swimming Eurypterus over pale mud in shallow olive water, with a restrained brass sun reflection.

options.label: Clear sunlit water
options.vo: Three: clear, sunlit, wide open water.
options.image_prompt: Clear sunlit Silurian seawater over an open pale sand bed. Close foreground sand ripple ridges and a few small flat mineral pebbles have crisp natural texture; the unobstructed pale seabed extends to the far blue-green water. Soft caustic sunlight moves over the ripples and makes a restrained warm brass reflection on one near pebble. Unoccupied natural-history underwater landscape, only mineral sediment, clear water and light.
options.art_direction: Clear blue-green shallow water above pale rippled sediment, warm reflected sunlight and readable mineral texture.

options.label: Twilight water, sixty metres
options.vo: Four: dim green twilight at sixty metres.
options.image_prompt: Close oblique underwater view across a large natural grey-green mudstone ledge on a Silurian shelf at sixty metres. The rock fills the lower four fifths of the image, with crisp fractured layers, fine shallow cracks, small pale shell fragments and irregular mineral grains. A narrow upper strip shows dim soft olive-green twilight water and fine suspended silt. Diffuse green light makes the nearby uneven rock texture readable, with a restrained warm amber reflection on one small near mineral chip. Only rock, shell fragments, sediment and submerged water.
options.art_direction: Close textured grey-green mudstone ledge filling most of the frame, dim olive twilight water above and a small restrained brass mineral reflection.

options.label: Pitch black, no light
options.vo: Five: deep enough that light gives up.
options.image_prompt: Straight downward close view of a rough natural mudstone outcrop on the seafloor in pitch black deep water. The rock surface fills nearly the complete frame with crisp angular fracture ridges, irregular charcoal mineral grains and pale silt collected in deep narrow cracks. A tiny upper corner opens beyond a broken rock edge into empty dark water. Soft neutral external documentary fill reveals the close rock and its matte pale mineral flecks. The surface is uneven natural stone with no animal or plant. This is an illustrative close geological detail.
options.art_direction: Downward close geological detail of crisp fractured charcoal mudstone with pale mineral flecks under soft neutral external documentary fill.

options.label: Cold silt bottom
options.vo: Six: the cold silt floor, blind.
options.image_prompt: Straight downward close view of a cold silty seafloor in pitch black deep water. Continuous fine matte grey mud fills the complete frame from corner to corner. Two shallow winding animal trackways and small low sediment ripple ridges cross the near silt diagonally. Crisp tiny mineral grains and small scattered mud clumps remain natural and uneven. Soft neutral external documentary fill reveals only this close patch of sediment. The open dark water lies outside this tight downward view. Only undisturbed mineral sediment and tracks are visible.
options.art_direction: Downward close-up of continuous cold grey silt and shallow winding trackways filling the complete frame under soft external documentary fill.

options.label: Beside the claw burrows
options.vo: Seven: next to a nest of claws.
options.image_prompt: A close underwater detail of two pairs of large brown Pterygotus cheliceral pincers resting on a flat muddy rock ledge. The animals remain completely behind the ledge, outside this close view. Four slender jointed claw arms enter from the upper edge in two separate pairs. Each ends in two narrow curved fingers with interlocking small teeth along their inner edges, matching the supplied claw-shape guide. The pincer teeth belong only to the claws. All the surrounding mud and mineral ledge are continuous unbroken natural surfaces. Fine silt curls around the claw tips in green Silurian water. Neutral documentary fill with one restrained warm amber glow on a near pincer, no visible head or body.
options.art_direction: Close submerged muddy ledge with two separate pairs of brown toothed pincers entering from above, olive-green water and a restrained brass reflection.

options.label: Eye to eye, Pterygotus
options.vo: Eight: face to face with Pterygotus.
options.image_prompt: Close three-quarter underwater portrait of one living Pterygotus, showing only its flat head shield and the bases of its two large cheliceral pincers. Use the supplied crop only as a head-and-claw shape guide, and follow the fossil-informed plan: a broad low trapezoid head shield with rounded corners, two large dark compound eyes at the front outer corners and a continuous matte brown carapace. The head is horizontal in the water. Two slender jointed pincers extend to the lower sides of the frame, with small interlocking teeth along the narrow curved fingers. The abdomen and small walking legs remain outside the tight portrait. Fine suspended silt in murky green Silurian water and neutral soft fill with a restrained warm amber glow reflected on the near eye. Natural non-glowing eyes.
options.art_direction: Tight horizontal Pterygotus head portrait with dark lateral compound eyes and slender toothed pincers in murky green water, restrained brass eye reflection.

original.verdict_vo: Real answer: number 5, because Pterygotus hunted with claws and sharp eyesight. Where the light runs out, a sight hunter probably loses you.

fact.text: Pterygotus was a large, active predator with big grasping claws and sharp vision comparable to modern predatory arthropods.
fact.source_sentence: Like its close relative Jaekelopterus, Pterygotus was a large and active predator noted for its robust and enlarged cheliceral claws that would have allowed it to puncture and grasp prey and a visual acuity (clarity of vision) comparable to that of modern predatory arthropods.

original.description:
Sea scorpions grew to monstrous sizes in these waters, and they hunted by sight. Pick your depth carefully.

Eurypterus reference: Susan H Butts, Eurypterus remipes (YPM IP 211408).jpg, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Eurypterus_remipes_(YPM_IP_211408).jpg (CC0, https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/), museum fossil shape guide adapted into an AI life reconstruction with illustrative colour and soft tissue / Pterygotus reference: Paleobiome, Pterygotus in enviroment.jpg, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pterygotus_in_enviroment.jpg (CC0, https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/), head and cheliceral-claw crop of a modern illustrative reconstruction, not fossil evidence adapted into an AI life reconstruction with illustrative colour and soft tissue

Show a pair of these brown armoured pincers resting side by side along the natural muddy floor, extending horizontally from a low shaded rock recess at the right. One near claw is fully visible in the same side view as the reference; the other lies partly behind it. Their short visible bases disappear naturally into the recess. Close low side-on underwater view, fine grey mud grains, olive-green Silurian water, a restrained warm brass reflection on the near shell and soft neutral fill. Preserve the reference pincer finger geometry; the rock and sediment have continuous plain natural surfaces.
options.art_direction: Preserve the supplied anatomical profile, matte natural surfaces, soft neutral fill and a restrained warm amber reflection in the established prehistoric palette

Keep the shield outline, relative eye size and lateral eye position, shell segmentation and joint placement as in the reference. A close living head and shoulder portrait retains the same proportions and orientation, with two brown armoured pincers extending forward horizontally. Natural finely pebbled matte brown shell and dark non-glowing lateral compound eyes. Replace the surrounding rock field with murky olive-green Silurian water and a softly defocused submerged mudstone slope. Soft neutral documentary fill and a restrained warm brass reflection on the shell. Change colour and surroundings, preserving the reference animal geometry.
